description: Historical example: the operations that turned one real team doc into its v3 (23 Nov 2026). The text values describe that day's setup and are not current facts; copy the shape, not the wording.

operations.text: QA Agent Ecosystem  |  QA Automation Workflow

operations.at: How reusable QA instructions reduce setup work while keeping review in the team.
operations.text: How reusable QA instructions, an independent reviewer and a shared lesson log reduce setup work while keeping review in the team.
On my setup, when a request can be read more than one way, the agent first restates what it understood, so the reader can correct it before any work is done.

QA judgement remains essential, and it is now backed by a second check. The agent confirms unclear requests, does the work, and reviewer-agent reviews it before hand-over. A person then approves the output. Every confirmed bug, mistake or instruction becomes a bug-investigator case with a prevention rule. reviewer-agent reviews the draft rule and I approve it before it is written into the relevant .md reference, so later runs follow it.

items.text: In its first review (23 Nov 2026), reviewer-agent found 5 issues in the agent’s own work, including one mistake the agent had repeated. All were fixed before hand-over.

Every review is recorded in a trust ledger: issues found, issues fixed, issues I confirmed, and issues I found that reviewer-agent missed. The missed count is the main signal for when a task can be automated further.
1.  Open the repo in VS Code, then open Claude Code.
2.  Type /qa-agent and describe the task in English.
3.  Review the generated output before reporting or using it.

On my setup the agent also restates unclear requests first, attaches a reviewer-agent verdict to every hand-over, and logs corrections as bug-investigator cases (reviewer-agent reviews each new rule and I approve it). These are not in the shared qa-agent repo yet: its coding-partner is still v1.0 (20 Nov 2026), and bug-investigator and reviewer-agent are not included.

qa-agent no longer works alone. Four agents now share the work: one does the QA, one holds the coding standards, one remembers every lesson, and one reviews the result before a person sees it. A QA reviewer still has the final say. bug-investigator, reviewer-agent and the newest coding-partner rules currently run on my setup only.

Each agent is a set of .md instructions. Two hooks keep them connected: every session starts with the latest lessons, and a message with bug or correction keywords reminds the agent to load bug-investigator.

rows: Validation and QA: runs suites safely, triages failures, automates pages, Figma checks, test cases
Coding standards: OOP and config-driven code, no comments, safe changes, the exact command to run. On my setup it also restates an unclear request before acting
Bug investigation and memory: finds the cause from evidence, logs every bug, mistake and instruction as a case with a prevention rule
A failure, a “why”, or a correction
Reviewer (crosscheck): an independent, read-only review of the agent’s work against our standards and past cases
Before any non-trivial work is handed over
